issues.detail: The Greek 'εν τω υψει αυτου' (in his height/exaltation) refers to the state or position of the person, but the Vietnamese 'về sự cao trọng của mình' (about their own honor/prestige) shifts the focus slightly. More importantly, the Greek 'καυχασθω' is an imperative/hortatory, but the Vietnamese 'Hãy để... khoe mình' (Let... boast) changes the subject of the action from the brother directly boasting to a passive construction where someone else allows the brother to boast.
